log.finding: NO_BUILDABLE_INPROCESS_MECHANISM_EXISTS. The genuine mechanism (ruleset-freshness-host.mjs) is itself only a local spawn of /usr/bin/git from whatever process it is running in -- it does not itself cross any sandbox boundary. Its own header comment states this explicitly: 'The caller is responsible for placing this executable on the boundary selected by pipeline-start. Running it from an ordinary workspace sandbox conveys no host attestation; the normal freshness CLI therefore never invokes this helper by itself.' The actual boundary-crossing step is external to this codebase: some other actor (the calling Codex session's own tool-call/exec layer) must already be running ruleset-freshness-host.mjs's process at a genuinely different (network-open) execution tier BEFORE any of this JS code starts. codex-app-server-health.mjs's observeCodexAppServer only execs 'codex app-server daemon version/restart' (a local health/version query, itself a child of the current, possibly-sandboxed process) -- no RPC exists anywhere in this codebase to submit a command for execution at a different network posture. codex-app-server-model-probe.mjs reveals the one genuine App-Server JSON-RPC surface present (initialize / thread/start with a sandbox parameter) but that starts a conversational model thread, spawned as a further child of the current process (inheriting its sandbox, per general OS process-inheritance -- not independently verified for this specific App-Server binary), not a command-execution delegation channel; examined and rejected as a candidate, not silently skipped. Confirmed by exhaustive precedent check: every other executionBoundary value in the codebase (local-process, attended-host-terminal, external-operator, separate-session-rooted-at-plugin-cache, separate-tool-call) is consumed identically -- as a label inside a returned nextAction/applyAction object instructing an EXTERNAL actor (human or the calling agent's own tool-tier choice) to run the given executable/argv at that boundary; none is consumed by in-process JS code to actually cross a sandbox. SKILL.md:65-67 confirms this reading explicitly: 'submit the exact returned action directly at that boundary' is agent-level tool-tier selection. docs/phoenix-governance-threat-model.md:53-57 states this as an explicit, direct operating rule, not just an inference: 'The in-process plan builder is not an executor. A host integration may execute only the returned action through its sanctioned read-only/network-open boundary and must pass the matching host transport to the normal freshness entrypoint.' This is the strongest single citation for the finding. Matches the briefing's second named stop condition exactly.
